findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: Adding an abstract method to a public SPI interface without a default implementation means any external/custom grant type provider implementing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory will no longer compile, and existing binary providers will throw AbstractMethodError when getShortcut() is invoked during DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(). Add a backward-compatible default method or otherwise handle factories that do not provide a shortcut.

findings.title: Access token jti claim changes from UUID to prefixed ID
findings.body: token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx)) now emits values like onrtac:<uuid> instead of the previous plain UUID. The jti claim is visible in issued access tokens and is often logged or treated as a UUID by clients and tests. This is an intentional format change, but it is a public token contract change that can break existing consumers that expect a 36-character UUID and should be called out as a migration/release-note concern.

findings.title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"), duplicating the grantType check and never checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted, and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId() will produce a token ID ending in ":null", violating the expected unique-ID format for jti. The check should requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

findings.title: Decoder assumes 2-char grant shortcut but the SPI permits longer shortcuts
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId() rejects any encoded context whose prefix length is not 6 and splits the prefix into three two-character parts. However OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() is documented as 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' and is never validated to be exactly two characters. A custom grant provider returning a three-character shortcut will be encoded successfully as, for example, onrtabc:<uuid> with a 7-character context prefix, but the same token will later fail to parse here with IllegalArgumentException. Validate shortcut length/format in postInit or encoding, or make the decoder handle the documented contract.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher extracts the wrong characters and has inverted assertion
findings.body: The grant type shortcut is positions 4-5, so it should be substring(4, 6), but the matcher uses substring(3, 5), which captures the second token-type character and the first grant-type character. It also returns false when that value equals the expected shortcut. As a result, the matcher does not actually verify the grant type and returns true for any access token whose suffix is a UUID and whose prefix has at least five characters. Tests using this matcher will not catch incorrect grant-type encoding. Fix the substring, remove the inverted return, and add a prefix-length check.

findings.title: Removed public Context copy constructor breaks custom grant implementations
findings.body: The public OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context context) copy constructor was removed. Custom grant type implementations or tests that construct a context from an existing context will no longer compile, and existing binary consumers referencing that constructor will fail. If the constructor is removed intentionally, this is a breaking SPI change that should be documented; otherwise retain a deprecated copy constructor that also copies the new grantType field.
